title: Investor Renovation Services | Genstone Construction
metaDescription: Renovation services for real estate investors: fix and flip, BRRRR, rentals, 2–4 units, REO and FHA 203(k), scoped around your strategy, budget and exit.
h1: Investor Renovation Services Built Around Your Strategy
lede: Selling the house after the work is done and holding it as a rental for years call for different renovations, even when the house is the same. Genstone Construction plans and executes renovations around the property, the budget, the timeline and the investment strategy, so the money goes where it moves your numbers and stays out of places that only look good on a walkthrough.

sections.body:
Two investors can walk through the same three-bedroom house and write completely different scopes, and both can be right. A flipper is writing for the buyer who tours on a weekend afternoon and the appraiser that buyer's lender sends out. A buy-and-hold investor is writing for the next ten years of tenants, turnovers and maintenance calls. The house hasn't changed. What the renovation needs to accomplish has.

That is why Genstone Construction starts with what you intend to do with the asset before it starts pricing anything. We develop detailed project scopes around the property, the budget and the intended use, so you understand the renovation priorities before work begins. Where it makes sense, we also lay out renovation options tied to projected after repair value (ARV), the budget you have available and the plan for the property, so you can see the trade-offs side by side instead of discovering them halfway through the job.

Throughout the project, the team focuses on clear communication, documentation, quality workmanship and disciplined execution. The goal is simple: the renovation that gets built should be the one you planned and paid for.

sections.h2: Fix and flip: buyer appeal, speed and project economics
sections.body:
A flip moves from acquisition to market-ready, and every day in between costs you interest, insurance, utilities and taxes. Renovation planning for a flip is about putting money where buyers notice it and where the comparable sales justify it, then executing fast enough that carrying costs don't eat the margin.

In practice that usually means the kitchen and baths get the most attention, flooring and paint run consistently through the house, curb appeal is handled early, and the systems an inspector will write up (roof, electrical panel, water heater, HVAC, visible plumbing) are dealt with before a buyer's inspection turns them into a renegotiation. Finish levels follow the neighborhood. Over-improving past what nearby renovated sales support is one of the most common ways a flip loses money, and under-finishing in an area where every comp has quartz and new cabinets leaves the house sitting.

Genstone's fix and flip work is planned around buyer appeal, timelines, budgets and the overall project economics, with the scope written so you can see what each line item contributes to the finished value.

sections.h2: BRRRR and rentals: durability and the refinance
sections.body:
A BRRRR project (buy, rehab, rent, refinance, repeat) has two audiences: the appraiser who sets the refinance value and the tenants who will live in the house afterward. The renovation has to support both.

For the refinance, the finished house needs to compare well against renovated sales in the area, so the scope still has to hit the features an appraiser weighs. For the tenancy, the materials have to hold up. That shifts choices toward luxury vinyl plank over carpet in most rooms, durable and easy-to-match paint colors, solid-surface or stone countertops that survive move-outs, quality faucets and supply lines, and mechanical systems with enough life left that you aren't replacing them in the second year of the hold.

Genstone creates rental-ready properties with durable, market-appropriate improvements designed to strengthen renter appeal, reduce avoidable maintenance and support long-term ownership. The same thinking applies to single-family rentals bought for straight buy-and-hold, small multifamily buildings of two to four units, and rental turns between tenants.

sections.h2: Other investor work we take on
sections.body:
Flips and BRRRR projects are the most common requests, but investor renovation covers more ground than that. Genstone's work also includes:

- Single-family rental renovations, including portfolio work where several houses need to come up to one consistent standard.
- Small multifamily properties with two to four units, where shared systems, separate meters and occupied units change how a job is phased.
- REO and bank-owned properties for mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and other lenders. Genstone is a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises.
- FHA 203(k) renovations. Genstone is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor and works with buyers, agents, consultants and lenders on standard and limited 203(k) projects.
- Rental turns and make-ready work between tenants.

Clients include individual investors as well as mortgage servicers, REITs, investment funds, banks and other mortgage lenders, so the systems behind each project are built for documentation and reporting, not just for getting the work done.

Every Genstone project follows the same three stages, whether it's a single house or one property in a larger portfolio.

Evaluate the property. Understand the anticipated renovation needs before you commit capital. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review estimates repair costs, helps refine the ARV, and checks whether the numbers support your offer while you can still walk away or adjust the price.

Build the scope. Once you move forward, you receive a detailed scope document and estimate covering labor, materials and the draw schedule. Many projects get more than one plan, with different finish levels matched to different ARV targets, so you can choose how far to take the house.

Execute the renovation. A designated field manager or project manager runs the project from start to finish. Permits, inspections, lien waivers and contractor compliance are handled as part of the job, and progress, documentation and milestones stay visible to you without a trip to the site. Final billing comes at the end, after completion and your approval.

Genstone does not take upfront payment. Construction draws are tied to completed work, so you pay for progress that has actually happened in the house. Final payment is due only after the project is complete and you've approved it.

That structure matters to investors for a few reasons. It keeps your cash available for acquisition, holding costs and reserves instead of sitting in a contractor's account. It lines up with the way most investor lenders fund rehab draws, which also release money against completed work after an inspection. And it gives everyone on the project the same incentive: finish the work that was scoped, document it, and move to the next stage.

Dumpster and debris removal costs are included in the estimate rather than added later, and completed work carries a one-year workmanship warranty. Damage caused by tenants and normal wear and tear are not covered by the warranty, which is worth knowing if the property will be leased soon after completion.

Genstone Construction is headquartered in Romeoville, Illinois, and coordinates a network of thousands of licensed and insured contractors. In each market, the work is performed by vetted local contractors who know the housing stock and the building department, while scoping, project management, documentation and billing follow one national standard.

For an investor who owns in more than one city, that means the scope format, the draw process and the reporting look the same from one property to the next. For an investor focused on one market, it means the crew on site is local while the process around them is built for investors.

The team behind each project includes estimators, field managers, repair specialists and billing staff. The executive team brings more than 60 years of combined construction experience across REO, fix-and-flip and single-family remodeling. Genstone has been named to the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies two years in a row and received Best of Houzz 2025 for Service.

If you're considering a property for purchase, start with a complimentary Pre-Offer Rehab Review. It gives you an estimate of the anticipated renovation needs and costs before you make an offer, a second look at the ARV, and a clearer read on whether the deal works at the price you have in mind.

You can request a review through the contact page or by calling (312) 429-2637. If you already own the property and are ready to renovate, the same conversation leads straight into a detailed scope and estimate.

faqs.q: Which investment strategies does Genstone renovate for?
faqs.a: Fix and flip, BRRRR, single-family rentals, small multifamily properties of two to four units, REO and bank-owned properties, FHA 203(k) renovations and rental turns. The scope is written differently for each, because a property headed for resale and a property headed for a long hold need different finishes and different priorities.

faqs.q: Can I get more than one scope option for the same property?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Where it's useful, Genstone develops renovation plans at different finish levels tied to different ARV targets, so you can compare what each level costs against what it should add to the finished value before you choose.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay anything before work starts?
faqs.a: No. There's no upfront payment. Construction draws are tied to completed work, and the final payment is due after the project is complete and you've approved it.
